walkthroughs.body_html:
Auxin moves to the shaded side of a shoot.

Auxin makes cells elongate. Shaded cells grow longer → shoot bends towards light. Roots respond oppositely so they grow down.

Auxins: rooting powders, weedkillers, tissue culture.

Gibberellins: end seed dormancy. Ethene: ripens fruit during transport. can ask you to match a hormone to a use.

Physical: waxy cuticle, thorns, bark. Chemical: antibacterial compounds, foxglove poisons.

Tobacco mosaic virus damages chloroplasts — leaves mottle, photosynthesis drops, yield falls.

mcqs.q: Where do plants get most of their biomass from?
options: From carbon dioxide in the air — the carbon in plant tissue comes mostly from CO2 fixed during photosynthesis.
Plants get most of their mass from the soil through their roots.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.

mcqs.q: How do hormones reach their target organs?
options: Hormones are sent through nerves directly to specific organs.
Hormones are released directly into target organs by being injected by glands.
Plants gain most of their mass directly from sunlight, which has weight.
They are carried in the bloodstream and act on cells with specific receptors for that hormone.
